evals.prompt: I'm the development director at Cascade Ballet Theatre in Tacoma — $3M budget, four productions a year including a Nutcracker that draws about 22,000 people. We've never had a season presenter; right now we just have a few $2,500 'friends of the ballet' business donors. Our 2027-28 season gets announced next April. Help me build a sponsorship program: what to sell, how to price it, and what the pitch should look like.
evals.expected_output: A sponsorship ladder (season presenter, production, program, day/event) with a benefits matrix across visibility, hospitality, engagement and affiliation, pricing that holds ladder arithmetic and exceeds benefits' fair market value, multi-year default terms, a prospect/category map and a one-pager structure, with tax-line cautions and CPA review.
assertions: Proposes an underwriting ladder of distinct properties (season presenter, production sponsor, program sponsor, day/event sponsor) with credit conventions, pricing the season deal at a multiple of a single production deal
Builds a benefits matrix across visibility, hospitality, engagement and affiliation, valuing each benefit by both org marginal cost and sponsor perceived value
Requires each tier's price to exceed the fair market value of its benefits and makes a multi-year commitment (with a modest term discount) the default ask

Recommends a category-mapped prospect list tagged by sponsor objective (awareness, client entertainment, employee engagement/CSR, community positioning) and a one-page leave-behind including a mocked-up credit visual
Explains the qualified sponsorship vs. advertising line (neutral acknowledgment, no qualitative/price language) and recommends routing the QSP/UBI split through the org's CPA before signature

evals.prompt: Our production sponsor (a local credit union, $15k) just sent playbill copy: 'Summit CU — lowest auto loan rates in the valley! Proud sponsor of Annie.' They also want to pay '$2 per ticket sold' next year instead of a flat fee. ok to just run it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the qualitative and price language converts acknowledgment into advertising (potential UBI) and proposes neutral credit language, that per-ticket contingent payments are never qualified sponsorship payments so a flat fee is needed, and recommends CPA review and a no-advertising clause in the agreement.
assertions: Identifies qualitative or price claims (e.g., 'lowest rates') as advertising rather than acknowledgment, making that revenue potentially taxable unrelated business income
Offers a neutral replacement credit line (e.g., name/logo with 'sponsored by')
States that payments contingent on attendance or tickets sold cannot be qualified sponsorship payments and recommends a flat fee
Recommends a no-advertising clause in the sponsorship agreement and routing the tax treatment to the org's CPA

evals.prompt: A regional hospital system wants to be our season presenter for $120K/year — huge for us (community theater, $1.1M budget, Iowa). But their VP mentioned they'd 'love input' on whether we do a play with an abortion storyline next spring, they want to be the 'official healthcare partner' while another clinic already sponsors our sensory-friendly shows, and they also floated putting their name on our lobby permanently as part of the deal. How do I handle this?
evals.expected_output: Insists on a written no-artistic-control clause, defines the exclusivity category precisely with a carve-out for the existing clinic relationship and notes exclusivity affects the QSP calculation, separates permanent lobby naming into a capital-campaign process rather than season-sponsorship pricing, and recommends staff/CPA review before signing or announcing.
assertions: Recommends an explicit written clause that the sponsor has no approval over content, casting or programming, and does not accept sponsor input on the title choice
Addresses exclusivity by defining the category precisely with a named carve-out for the existing clinic sponsor

Notes that with exclusivity only the portion of payment exceeding the fair market value of exclusivity and other benefits is a qualified sponsorship payment, and that the estimate should be documented
Separates permanent lobby naming from the season deal, routing it to nonprofit-capital-campaigns and warning not to price it on season-sponsorship logic
Advises not publishing the presenter credit until the agreement is signed and recommends knowledgeable staff/CPA review

should_not_trigger.query: We want to sell naming rights to our new black-box theater as part of our $6M building campaign — how do we value it?
Design a corporate partnership strategy and cause-marketing program with a national retailer for our youth orchestra.
